scoring.headline: runners/lmc-runner weighted accuracy (Completion 0.32, BugFix 0.22, Refactor 0.12, TestGen 0.10, FeatureAdd 0.10, ApiDiscovery 0.14, renormalized over categories present)
scoring.strict_absence: contains with an empty required list scores 0 when the adapter returns any id; the headline scorer scores that case 1
scoring.latency: adapter wall time, P50/P95/P99 via the runner nearest-rank percentile
scoring.compression_ratio: symbol-card catalog tokens / mean returned stable-id tokens
scoring.cost: retrieval cost_usd is 0 except Hindsight reflect, which is reported separately and is not mixed into weighted accuracy

index.query_rendering: bare-name lookup uses the symbol name; full-id lookup uses the trailing identifiers with the symbol first; file_symbols uses the path tail (filename stem first, extensions shorter than 3 characters omitted) so a 5-token keyword window still sees the distinctive segments; structural ops use the trailing identifier. The same string is sent to every system.
index.symbol_cards: One memory per stable id that appears in that corpus's scenario file (expected ids and queried sym ids). Cards store the bare name, a suffix kind hint, path segments parsed from the id, and the id. They do not store the per-query expected list.
index.source_trees: not cloned; published scenario files are the suite

mechanism.temporal_wiring: Published scenarios have no commit timestamps. Every symbol card already carries at and at_ord from index build (stable-id order within the corpus, encoded as 2020-01-01T00:00:00.{ordinal}Z). Code queries contain no askedAt and no Chinese time words. The temporal channel still runs for every query: asked time is the newest at in that query's corpus, and the channel returns the 10 cards closest to it. Graph temporal edges use the paper's 24h window; the whole catalog spans well under 24h, so those edges are complete and the spread uses that closed form. Same-corpus entity edges (weight 0.6) stay below that temporal spread and do not change the top of the graph channel.
mechanism.latency_note: Per-query latency is fusion + cross-encoder wall time, plus the median single-query MiniLM encode measured on 24 warm calls. Document vectors are built once and are not included.
